assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only cornered-mouse:natsuki@manga#character-monograph, the active_provisional CORNERED_MOUSE_NATSUKI_MONOGRAPH at basis_commit, read in full: its argument over Natsuki's material scenes in CM-U04 (sp0100-sp0137), CM-U06 (sp0143-sp0204) and the CM-S01 closing comic (sp0535) of the revised Japanese witness CM-JP-AIO2020-LOCAL, as the monograph reports them. The CM-U04, CM-U06 and CM-S01 readings it links are not curated on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them; the corpus readiness review it links is a method input, not evidence. The Reboot-only story, other editions and adaptations are outside, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Three placed horizons: the CM-U04 encounter (her account of the earlier breakup and the lighter), the CM-U06 sequence (renewed proposal, refusal to withdraw, cafe choice, refused confession, holiday booking and unanswered call), and the closing comic's reported later marriage, which the monograph places after Hummingbird only through a creator note. The interval between the unanswered call and the closing report is unshown and not assessed; no other state is assessed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph argues one recurring want across CM-U04 and CM-U06, to be actively chosen rather than kindly tolerated: her counter-account of the earlier breakup (sp0116-0117), the renewed proposal (sp0144), the refusal to withdraw for Imagase (sp0151, sp0154), the refused confession meant for the absent man (sp0163-0164) and the holiday booking and call (sp0176, sp0200). It is tested against the authoritative-interpreter and mere-obstacle readings. C is rejected because no conditional rule is derived and the scenes are all interested romantic crises; E is rejected because the disposition is argued across two units with located countercases. This is the closest call in the record.

Three horizons are placed (CM-U04, CM-U06, closing report), but the monograph states the call aftermath is unshown and the later marriage is reported, not enacted. No development between states is traced, so D is rejected.

Located voice evidence is limited to her named idioms, the ditch and piper/mouse metaphors (sp0155, sp0158), and gendered judgments in the closing banter (sp0535). Her Japanese is paraphrased and no register analysis is given.

Ordinary conduct is limited to booking, confirming and calling about a holiday (sp0176, sp0200) and the bag envy in the closing comic. Each is embedded in a romantic contest; no neutral daily behavior is analyzed.

Two counterparts are differentiated within one triangle: the demand on Kyoichi and the refusal to yield to Imagase, plus later abrasive familiarity with Imagase (sp0535). The monograph states that no neutral, private or occupational relation is available, so D is rejected.

Interior states are spoken: she kept loving him but felt unloved (sp0117), and her dissatisfaction at being the wrong audience for his confession (sp0164). The monograph refuses to treat her as a neutral witness or to diagnose her.

Located conflict: the lighter disagreement (sp0115), refusing Imagase's plea (sp0151-0154), injuring metaphors (sp0155-0158), the cafe frame (sp0160-0161) and the refused confession. D is rejected because these are all one triangle across a few scenes, without a stated pattern of escalation or repair.

She gives a reason for refusing to withdraw (she chose Kyoichi and will forgive unless he ends it, sp0154) and sets a boundary on receiving his confession. The monograph's ethical analysis is mostly its own account of her injuring language and gendered assumptions, so only E is supported.
One located instance: the closing comic's abrasive banter with Imagase, which the monograph calls interested banter (sp0535). No other play is analyzed.

One 56-line monograph over the complete supplied witness. The unit readings it cites are not curated on the row, so the evaluator could not check its locators, and her coverage is limited to scenes in which she is material.

Affirmative limits are located: her forceful-kiss wish is her stated fantasy and cannot be a rule for reading refusal (sp0117); the old marriage thought is a past possibility, not an engagement (sp0144); her questions give her knowledge of an issue, not every household term (sp0145); the call aftermath is unshown; and the monograph records that the corpus review withholds a portable behavioral model.
Scenes are placed by unit and spine, but the closing report's chronology rests on a creator note, the gap after the call is open, and no calendar dating is given.

scenario_readiness.note: With paraphrased speech and only two named idioms, generated lines would be fluent invention rather than source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not Natsuki's speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The CM-U04 encounter or the CM-U06 sequence up to the unanswered holiday call; the reported later marriage is not an enacted state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kyoichi as former partner she is trying to win back, or Imagase as rival; the refusal applies equally to any other counterpart.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts beyond the located scenes
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than bounded canon description

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph withholds a portable model because her scenes are interested romantic contests without a neutral baseline.
The monograph states that no repeated neutral or private baseline exists; the holiday logistics are part of the romantic contest.
One stated reason and one boundary, alongside injuring judgments the monograph declines to resolve, give no procedure for novel ethical choices.

Romance is the bulk of the evidence, but the monograph keeps her account of the past as one narrator's, refuses to make her fantasy a consent rule, leaves the call aftermath unshown and gives only a reported later marriage. Simulating it would supply Kyoichi's missing answer.
The monograph names the absence of any occupational baseline as a reason the corpus review withholds a model; this is an evidenced insufficiency, not inference from silence.

known_limits.statement: Every analyzed scene is an interested romantic contest over Kyoichi; the monograph records that no repeated neutral, private or occupational baseline exists and that the corpus review withholds a portable behavioral model.
Her wish for a forceful kiss despite refusal is her stated fantasy about their relation and cannot become a general instruction for reading refusal as desire or supplying anyone's consent.

The title-work ending shows no answered call, cancellation or honest breakup with her; the closing comic's marriage to a younger man is a report that does not fill that gap, and its placement rests on a creator note.
Her account of the earlier breakup corrects Kyoichi's but is one narrator's interpretation; she is not a neutral witness to every part of him, and her metaphors and gendered judgments are interested.
The CM-U04, CM-U06 and CM-S01 readings the monograph cites are not curated on this subject, so its locators and paraphrases were not checked against them. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
The monograph paraphrases Natsuki's Japanese, so self-reference, sentence endings and register are not in the curated evidence.
